AiMY QA Design System

Build consistent.
Ship confident.

Every token, component, and pattern used across AiMY QA v2, from the AI Chat canvas to the justifys audit trail. One source of truth so every surface feels native to the same product.

Use the tinted tag for status and metadata. Use a solid tag only for short, high-priority states. Solid semantic fills carry --text-on-status, which resolves to #0d1117 on the dark theme and #ffffff on the light one; purple keeps its existing treatment.
Surfaces

AiMY QA v2 has five distinct surfaces. Each has its own role model, layout, and interaction pattern, but all share the same token layer and component library.

🧠
Dashboard
Primary · AI-first
AI Chat canvas + briefing cards + goal feed. The primary surface for day-to-day supervisor work. Two-tier grid layout.
📋
Reviews
Drill-down · Performance
Team → Agent → Evaluation → Detail. Four-level drill-down for quality analysis. Mirrors canvas render templates.
⚙️
Goal Hub
Admin · Configuration
Template browser, metric registry, governance controls, metric health. 3 of 4 tabs role-gated to Admins only.
⚖️
justifys
Workflow · Role-based
Full lifecycle justify management. Three roles (Agent, Auditor, Admin) with distinct views, permissions, and SLA tracking.
🔌
Data Ingestion
Operations · Infrastructure
Pipeline health monitoring, voice file upload, and source configuration (Zendesk, Freshdesk, S3, AiMY Connect). Compliance-grade audit trail. API keys always masked.

Theming

Dark is the default. Light is <html data-theme="light">, resolved before first paint from localStorage["aimy-ds-theme"], falling back to the OS prefers-color-scheme. Use the switch in the top bar, or press Shift+D. Every override is token-level: no component forks its markup or its rules per theme.

◆
Light is not the dark theme inverted. The two themes signal depth by opposite means, so a mechanical flip produces a broken interface. Dark marks elevation by getting lighter; light keeps surfaces white and marks elevation with shadow. And the dark ramp’s accents cannot survive a white ground — they were chosen to glow against near-black.
Why the accents are re-derived, not reused — and what light ships now

The dark hues were chosen to glow against near-black and sit at 1.6–2.6:1 on white, so light cannot reuse them. What light ships is the bold family, restored to match Knowledge and Sales: hues bold enough to carry colour, which clear the 3:1 a border, dot, icon or tag edge answers to but not the 4.5:1 body copy needs. Where the hue has to set a sentence, the ink is --ok-text / --warn-text / --err-text / --info-text / --cyan-text — light’s deep set, which is the family this one replaced, re-pointed to the one role it is safe for. Measured on the card (#fff) and on the body (#eef1f6).

The three things that actually flip
LayerDarkLightWhy
Surface ramp
--d950 … --d750		 Ground #0f1215 → card #141b24 → raised #1c2630. Elevation = more light. Ground #eef1f6 → card #ffffff. Raised stays white. Once the card is white there is nowhere lighter to go, so elevation moves into --shadow-*.
Ink ramp
--d600 … --d50		 7 steps rising to #f5f7fb. 7 steps falling to #0f172a, each ~1.22× the last. Dark-on-light reads heavier than light-on-dark, so the steps are re-spaced rather than mirrored. Every step clears AA on card and ground.
Wash ramp
--w015 … --w50		 White at 1.5%–50% — every hairline, subtle fill and hover. Navy #0f172a at a re-tuned alpha. Hairlines hold their alpha because they need the presence; broad fills drop ~25% because dark-on-light reads heavier. Pure black washes look grey and dirty, so the wash is navy-tinted.
Deliberate exceptions
WhatBehaviourReason
Code blocks--code-bg and the --syn-* palette do not flip. Only --code-border changes.A snippet should read identically wherever it is quoted.
Colour specimensSwatches in Color Tokens and Preserved foundation stay pinned to their literal hex.They document the palette itself, so they must not move with the theme.
--text-on-status#0d1117 in dark, #ffffff in light.Solid status chips are bright in dark and deep in light, so the ink on them inverts.
--heat-inkNear-black in both themes.Heat-scale fills are saturated tints in both themes, so the ink does not follow --text-on-status.
Adding a surface to the theme
Rule of thumb
/* Never hardcode a surface, an ink or a hairline. */
.my-panel {
  background: var(--card-bg);        /* not #141b24 */
  color: var(--d200);               /* not #c3ceda */
  border: 1px solid var(--w07);    /* not rgba(255,255,255,0.07) */
  box-shadow: 0 4px 16px var(--shc-2); /* geometry yours, ink themed */
}

/* A tint keeps its alpha and swaps its hue through the -rgb token. */
.my-panel.is-error {
  background: rgba(var(--err-rgb), 0.09);
  color: var(--err);
}

Both themes are audited against their composited backgrounds, not their nominal ones. The contrast table re-measures itself whenever you switch, so the numbers there are always the live theme’s.

Typography

One typeface across all surfaces: Poppins (200–700) — body and titles alike, so --font-sans and --font-display name the same face. Code and token values use JetBrains Mono. Headings use negative tracking; labels use positive tracking.

Shell Structure
/* Three-zone shell, identical across all surfaces */
.app-shell {
  display: flex;
  padding-top: var(--topbar-height);
  min-height: 100vh;
}

.app-topnav {
  position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0;
  height: var(--topbar-height);
  z-index: 100;
  background: rgba(15,18,21,0.88);
  backdrop-filter: blur(24px);
}

.app-sidebar {
  width: var(--sidebar-width);
  position: fixed;
  top: var(--topbar-height); bottom: 0;
  overflow-y: auto;
}

.app-main {
  margin-left: var(--sidebar-width);
  flex: 1; min-width: 0;
  padding: 24px 32px 100px;
  overflow-y: auto;
}
Dashboard Grid
/* Tier 1, 4-column goal briefing row */
.tier-1-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);
  gap: 16px;
  margin-bottom: 16px;
}

/* Tier 2, asymmetric narrative + goal feed */
.tier-2-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1.5fr 1fr;
  gap: 16px;
  align-items: start;
}

Cards

Three card types. All share --card-bg and --card-border but have different anatomy, padding, and interaction. Only one card per dashboard may carry .tier-primary.

Briefing Card · .bcard

Primary information unit on the Dashboard. Each card has five structural zones stacked vertically inside .bcard-body: meta row (type label + priority badge) → conclusion sentence → evidence pills → divider → action row (.bcard-action). The action row (.bcard-action) is flex-direction:column, the primary .action-btn comes first, then the .expand-toggle sits below it. Below the body sits the collapsible .bcard-data grid (hidden by default, opened by the expand-toggle).

Briefing Card · Full Anatomy

The complete .bcard as used on the Dashboard. The simple variant (documented in Cards above) is the collapsed state. This section documents every sub-component: the conclusion + evidence zone, the action zone, the ack/dismiss row, and the expandable metric data panel.

ℹ
Only one .bcard per dashboard may carry .tier-primary, it elevates with a QA-accent glow ring to draw the eye to the most urgent alert first. The .is-acknowledged state auto-desaturates and sends the card to the visual back via CSS order: 99.

Friction Feed

A compound component on the Dashboard left column. The .signal-card is the AI-detected live friction event. It sits above a .feed-items strip of related secondary signals. Together they form the .friction-feed. The signal card has an expandable driver bar section that reveals the root-cause analysis.

ℹ
The .signal-card and .feed-items strip share a connected border. The card has no bottom border and the strip has no top radius. They always appear together, never separately. The full-bleed .raw-data-toggle button must live inside .signal-card (which has overflow:hidden) so it bleeds to the edges without needing negative margins.

AiMY Action Chips

Large, card-like chips surfaced by AiMY as prioritised action suggestions. Each chip has a severity tier (urgent, caution, explore) communicated through border tint, background tint, a 2px top-edge accent line, and a badge. Chips are dismissible, dismissal fires a toast with a 5-second undo window and feeds a learning signal back to AiMY.

All Variants
Three disputes past SLA Urgent

The oldest has been open 11 days.

Empathy drifting on Team Nile Caution

Down 8 points over three weeks.

A rubric change would settle 14 Explore

Most overturned justifys cite the same clause.

ModifierBorderBackgroundTop accentBadgeUse
.v2-chip.urgentrgba(err, 0.3)rgba(err, 0.04)--err.urgent-badge, err colorsRequires immediate action
.v2-chip.cautionrgba(warn, 0.3)rgba(warn, 0.04)--warn.caution-badge, warn colorsWatch / investigate
.v2-chip.explorergba(brand, 0.25)rgba(brand, 0.04)--ai gradient.explore-badge, blue tintAI-surfaced opportunity
.v2-chip.dismissed----Opacity 0, scale 0.95, pointer-events none, triggers undo toast

Donut Chart

SVG donut used for pass/fail/borderline breakdowns (Tickets Evaluation panel). Three visible arc segments, pass (green gradient), borderline (warn), fail (err), sit over an invisible track. A layer of transparent .donut-hit rings handles hover interactions without gap-flicker between segments. Active segment expands via stroke-width and gets a glow filter. Center text updates reactively via JS.

Arc geometry formula

circumference = 2π × r = 2π × 40 ≈ 251.3 · stroke-dasharray = (pct/100) × 251.3 · stroke-dashoffset = −(sum of all previous arcs)

Context Zone

A two-zone panel attached to the top of the AiMY canvas overlay. Zone 1 (--state) surfaces what AiMY has detected, the active state pill + alternative states the user can switch to. Zone 2 (--suggestions) shows the AiMY action chips keyed to that detected state. The two zones are always co-present: the detected state drives which chips appear. Changes to the detected state refresh the chips.

Accessibility

AiMY QA targets WCAG 2.1 AA. These are the non-negotiable rules, not aspirational guidelines. Every new component ships with these applied.

Focus Rings

Tab through the elements below to see the focus ring. Always --brand blue, never the QA accent, which is a placeholder and will change.

Nav link
Tab through elements above, focus ring: 2px solid var(--brand), offset 2px
/* Global focus, only :focus-visible, never :focus */
*:focus { outline: none; }

button:focus-visible,
a:focus-visible,
[role="button"]:focus-visible,
input:focus-visible,
select:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--brand);
  outline-offset: 2px;
  border-radius: var(--r-md);
}
Color Contrast

Ratios are measured against the active theme and recomputed when you switch, so both themes are held to the same bar. Minimum AA (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large/bold ≥18px or bold ≥14px).

ForegroundBackgroundRatioGradeUsed on
--d50 --card-bg - - Card titles, primary body text
--d300 --card-bg - - Secondary text, field labels, nav items
--d400 --card-bg - - Sub-labels, hints, only at 12px+ bold or 14px+
--ok --card-bg - - Pass labels, ok badge text
--warn --card-bg - - Warning labels, borderline badge text
--err --card-bg - - Error labels, fail badge text
--brand --card-bg - - Brand buttons (white text on top passes independently)
#ffffff --brand - - White text on .btn-brand, the primary CTA
--d500 --body-bg - - Captions and helper text on the page ground
--ai-ink --card-bg - - AI signals, links and inline AI labels
ARIA Patterns
ComponentRequired attributesNotes
Nav sidebarrole="navigation", aria-label="Main navigation"Active link: add aria-current="page"
Modalrole="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby="modal-title-id"Move focus to first focusable element on open. Return focus to trigger on close. Trap focus inside.
Toggle switchUse native <input type="checkbox">Label via visible <label> or aria-label. Never use a <div> alone.

Progress barrole="progressbar", aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin="0", aria-valuemax="100"Include aria-label with category name.
Icon-only buttonaria-label="descriptive action"Never rely on a tooltip alone to convey the action.
Live signal badgerole="status", aria-live="polite"Only use aria-live="assertive" for critical alerts (P1 justifys).
Masked API inputautocomplete="off", autocomplete="new-password"Prevents browser autofill from leaking credentials into the visible DOM.
Skeletonaria-busy="true" on the containerRemove when content loads. Announce with aria-live="polite" region.
Reduced Motion
ℹ
All animations and transitions must respect prefers-reduced-motion. The skeleton shimmer, signal dot blink, score ring fill, and card hover lifts are all animated, include the override below in your global stylesheet.
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after {
    animation-duration:   0.01ms !important;
    animation-iteration-count: 1     !important;
    transition-duration:  0.01ms !important;
    scroll-behavior:      auto   !important;
  }
}
⚠
QA Accent placeholder reminder: When --qa-accent is replaced with the real magenta from Figma, re-check focus ring contrast against --body-bg and --card-bg. The current purple (#8b4ff4) passes AA. The replacement must too.

Briefing Card — Aggregate

A briefing item whose subject is a cluster, not a record. The standard briefing card states one conclusion about one thing and backs it with evidence pills; that shape breaks when the finding is a distribution — thirty unanswered questions clustered by topic, failures spread across six sources. Here the evidence row is replaced by a ranked contributor list, because which things and how much each is the finding.

142 questions went unanswered this week because nothing in the corpus covers them. Four topics account for most of it.

ElementClassNotes
Variant.bcard.is-aggregateModifier on the standard briefing card — same meta row, conclusion, action row and ack/dismiss row. Only the evidence zone differs
Totals strip.agg-summary / .agg-statTwo or three figures at most: the total, the shape of the spread, and the trend. This is not a stat wall
Contributor list.agg-list / .agg-rowRanked, highest first. Four or five rows — past that the card is a table pretending to be a briefing item
Proportion bar.agg-barSet --agg-share from 0–1 relative to the top row. Renders behind the label with transform: scaleX(), never an animated width
Remainder.agg-moreRequired when the list is truncated. A ranked list that hides its tail overstates how concentrated the problem is
Action.entry-actionOne action for the cluster, classified like any other. It may act on the whole cluster or on the top contributor — say which in the label
The tail is part of the finding. Showing four topics out of thirteen without saying so turns a broad problem into a narrow one and sends the reader to fix the wrong thing. .agg-more is not optional decoration.
An aggregate card still owes everything a briefing item owes: what changed, why it matters, scope, work state, and one classified next step. Being a cluster is not an excuse to skip the conclusion sentence and lead with numbers.
Type Cards

Eight templates for eight kinds of knowledge object, sharing one fixed governance row. Type changes what a reader needs to see first — a Ticket without its resolution is useless, an ICP without its disqualifiers is misleading, a Success Story without its approval state is a legal exposure. A single template forces every type into the fields of whichever type it was designed around, and the fields that matter most end up in a drawer.

What never moves. Type · trust state · title · owner · last verified · one classified action sit in the same position on all eight templates. Someone scanning mixed results must not have to relearn where trust lives per type. Only the zone between the title and the governance row varies.

Compact form — .is-compact

What survives when a card is cited inside a host with far less width than the workbench. Title, type, trust state, one action — nothing else. This is a requirement of the template, not a host concern: if the compact form is not designed, the host will improvise one, and trust will be the field it drops.

Approval is a separate field, not a trust value — deliberately. Approval is not verification: a Success Story can be verified as accurate and still not be cleared for external use. Whether approval becomes a sixth trust value or stays its own field is an open question, so .tc-approval is kept outside .trust-state rather than pre-empting that decision. If the ruling makes it a trust value, this field folds in and the templates are unaffected.
Document Viewer

The reading shell for any knowledge object. Type-appropriate body, constant governance chrome. A viewer is not a read-only editor — it is optimised for judging and citing content rather than changing it, which is why trust sits above the body rather than in a details panel: the only ordering that helps someone decide whether to rely on the content is the one that tells them before they read it.

Version History & Restore

Where the correction loop terminates and where AI edits become reversible. Two rules shape the component: AI edits are ordinary versions with an AI author, and restore is a consequential write.

No parallel AI history. A separate track for AI edits lets someone review the human history and believe they have seen everything. AiMY's versions sit in the same list, marked by author — the same way the audit trail already refuses to disguise AiMY's actions as the user's.

Restore is additive. It creates a new version rather than deleting the ones it supersedes — otherwise restoring is itself an irreversible act, and the audit trail acquires a hole exactly where someone will later need to look.
Work State

What AiMY has actually done about a surfaced item. This is a required field on every briefing item, insight, recommendation and canvas response — not a decoration. Collapsing these values (for example showing "recommended" work as if it were already "staged") misrepresents how much agency the user still holds.

The six values

The underlying state is always one of six. They progress left to right; failed can terminate the sequence at any point.

Detected Recommended Drafted Staged Completed Failed
StateClassMeansUser still owes
detected.ws-detectedAiMY noticed a signal. No opinion formed yet.Nothing — read it
recommended.ws-recommendedAiMY has an opinion about what to do.Decide whether to act
drafted.ws-draftedAiMY produced content (a message, a plan, a config) but has not queued it.Read and edit
staged.ws-stagedThe action is prepared and waiting on a human decision.Approve or reject
completed.ws-completedThe action ran. Undo may still be available.Nothing
failed.ws-failedThe action was attempted and did not succeed, or could not be attempted.Retry or escalate
Display-label aliases

Domain language may rename two of the six on screen. The class and data-work-state must still carry the underlying value — analytics, filtering and the review gate read the attribute, not the label.

Handled data-work-state="completed"
Blocked data-work-state="failed"
Pipeline — .ws-track

Where an item sits in the sequence. Use on detail surfaces and in the canvas, not on every briefing card — the single badge is enough there.

Detected Recommended Drafted Staged Completed
ElementClassNotes
Badge.work-state + .ws-*9px/700 uppercase pill. Always carries data-work-state with one of the six canonical values
Dot.ws-dot6px. Filled for states AiMY has committed to (recommended, staged, completed, failed); hollow ring for observational states (detected, drafted)
Pipeline.ws-trackSteps are .ws-step with .is-past / .is-current; separators are .ws-sep
Never use color alone to carry the state — the label text is mandatory. Screen readers and monochrome contexts must still resolve which of the six applies. 
<!-- Canonical state on the attribute, domain label in the text -->
<span class="work-state ws-staged" data-work-state="staged">
  <span class="ws-dot"></span>Staged
</span>

<!-- "Handled" is a display alias for completed -->
<span class="work-state ws-completed" data-work-state="completed">
  <span class="ws-dot"></span>Handled
</span>
Trust State

Whether a piece of content can be relied on — and whether the AI is still allowed to answer from it. A required field on every knowledge object, and the one indicator that must survive leaving its home product: an expired card has to read as expired inside a consuming agent's canvas, inside an embedded panel, anywhere it is cited. A trust indicator that only renders at home is worse than none at all, because it teaches people that no warning means safe.

Trust state is not work state. Work state says what AiMY has done with an item; trust state says whether the item's content holds. An object can be drafted and expired at the same time — AiMY has proposed an update, and the content currently published is past review. Collapsing the two loses the distinction exactly where it carries the most weight.
The five values
Verified Due Expired Unverified Superseded
ValueClassMeansRetrieval
verified.ts-verifiedOwner confirmed within cadenceAvailable
due.ts-dueReview date approachingAvailable, flagged
expired.ts-expiredReview date passed without confirmationExcluded — add .is-excluded
unverified.ts-unverifiedNever verified, or ingested without an ownerAvailable, flagged prominently
superseded.ts-supersededReplaced by a newer objectExcluded — resolves to successor
Excluded from answers — .is-excluded

Exclusion is a consequence, so it is stated on the badge rather than left to a tooltip. Marking content stale while continuing to serve it produces a marking users correctly learn to ignore; exclusion is what gives the state teeth, and saying so is what keeps it honest.

Expired without the modifier — state only Expired with .is-excluded — state and consequence
On a knowledge object

Both axes on one card. The dot marks work state, the icon marks trust state — deliberately different shapes so a meta row carrying both does not read as one field split in two.

Portable by construction. Trust state uses semantic tokens only and never --accent. Embedded surfaces adopt the consuming agent's accent, so an accent-tinted trust badge would change meaning between products. Type and state are carried by label and icon together, never colour alone — both for contrast and because the colour system may differ where the card is cited. 
<!-- Canonical value on the attribute; .is-excluded when
     the state removes the content from retrieval -->
<span class="trust-state ts-expired is-excluded"
      data-trust-state="expired">
  <!-- slashed-circle icon -->
  Expired
</span>

<!-- Both axes coexist on one object -->
<span class="work-state ws-drafted"  data-work-state="drafted">…</span>
<span class="trust-state ts-expired" data-trust-state="expired">…</span>
Entry Modes

The same click must not always produce the same behaviour — so it must not always look the same. Every interactive element on a briefing surface is deliberately assigned one of four modes at design time, and the affordance tells the user which one they are about to get. An unclassified action is an incomplete design.

Direct Action Completes in place. Toast with Undo.
Automatic Investigation Canvas opens and starts reading immediately.
Prepared Prompt Canvas opens with the question staged. User sends.
Reviewed Action Shows a diff with Accept · Edit · Reject. Never silent.
Classification
ModeClassAssign whenReturns to
Direct action.em-directObvious, low-risk, one step. Do not open the canvas merely because it exists.Same state
Automatic investigation.em-investigateThe selected item implies a clear, read-only question.Same state, thread preserved
Prepared prompt.em-promptIntent is broader or interpretive — the user should shape the question.Same state, thread preserved
Reviewed action.em-reviewAiMY proposes a change with operational consequence.Same state, thread preserved
Design-time annotation — .entry-mode-tag

The dashed tag is a specification affordance, not production UI. Use it in design files and review decks so every action on a surface can be seen to carry a mode. Strip it from shipped screens.

What is the Aimy design system?
A shared token layer and component library that every Aimy product builds on, so surfaces feel native to the same family.
Can a product change the accent color?

Does it support light and dark?

Set-Scope Operations

Acting on many records at once — bulk verification, reassignment, expiry, retagging. The component exists for one reason: to state what the selection actually is before anything runs. "Apply to selected" hides blast radius at the exact moment blast radius is the only thing that matters, and a filtered selection is especially treacherous because the filter, not the user, chose most of what is in it.

Selection bar
18 selected of 240 cards · filtered to Policies, owner A. Mahfouz, trust state expired
Select-all across a filter selects the filter, not the page. Say which.
240 selected Every card matching the current filter, including 222 not shown on this page.
Effect preview

What the operation will do — including what it will skip. A bulk action that silently no-ops on part of its selection produces a success message the user has no reason to distrust.

18 selected of 240 cards · filtered to Policies, trust state expired
What this will do
Send a verification request to 6 owners covering 15 cards.
2 cards have no owner and will be routed to the collection lead instead.
1 card is superseded and will be skipped — its successor is already verified.
Reversible for 24h · logged to audit trail
Confirmation rung

Set-scope operations are multi-entity by definition, so they start at rung 2 and climb with consequence. The primary button names the operation and its count — never "Apply" or "Confirm".

OperationRungSurface
Retag, add to collection — reversible, no retrieval effect2Inline confirm in the bar
Reassign ownership, request verification2Effect preview + inline confirm
Bulk expire — removes content from answers3Effect preview + Decision Zone
Bulk delete, changing per-agent source exposure4Type-to-Confirm + Audit Trail
ElementClassNotes
Bar.set-scope-barAppears when a selection exists. Accent-bordered — it is a transient mode, not permanent chrome
Count.ss-count / .ss-numThe raw number, largest element in the bar
Scope statement.ss-scopeMandatory. Total, active filters, and whether the selection reaches beyond the visible page
Actions.ss-actionsOperations carry their entry mode like any other action
Effect preview.ss-preview / .ss-effect.is-ok will happen · .is-warn will happen differently than expected · .is-skip will not happen. All three are required where they apply
Never let a bulk operation report success for work it skipped. The skip line is not a nicety — it is the difference between "15 requests sent" and a user believing all 18 cards are handled.

Audit Trail

The answer to what did I do about this, and what happened next. Distinct from Timeline: a timeline narrates events, an audit trail attributes them. Every consequential action needs an entry naming the actor, the action, the time, and whether it can still be reversed. AiMY-originated entries are visually marked — the user must always be able to tell what they did from what the system did on their behalf.

AI Unavailable

A first-class designed state, not an afterthought. When AiMY cannot answer — the model is down, the quota is spent, or a downstream action is unreachable — the surface must say so plainly and hand the user something they can still do. Falling back to a spinner, a generic error, or an empty canvas is the failure this component exists to prevent.

Unavailable
AiMY can't answer right now

The reasoning service is unreachable. Your dashboard, filters and existing data are unaffected — only the conversation is down.

Your draft message is saved and will send when the service returns.
Degraded

Partial capability. Say precisely what still works — "AiMY is slow" tells the user nothing they can act on.

Running on reduced capability

AiMY can still read and explain your data. It cannot stage or apply actions until the action service recovers — proposals will be drafted and held.

Drafting only
Quota exhausted
Conversation limit reached for this cycle

Your workspace has used all 2,000 canvas conversations for July. Briefings, dashboards and structured workflows continue as normal.

Resets 1 August.
ElementClassNotes
Panel.ai-unavailableDashed border — this is an absence, not an error. .is-degraded switches to a solid warn border for partial capability
Mark.aiu-markDimmed #aimy-logo-small when AiMY is simply down; a semantic icon when the cause is known (quota, degraded)
Title.aiu-titleWhat is unavailable, in the user's terms. Not "Error 503"
Body.aiu-bodyMust state what still works. The dashboard being fine is the most useful thing you can tell someone here
Fallback.aiu-fallbackRetry plus at least one real destination. This is where a dead end would otherwise form
Note.aiu-noteWhat happens to work in flight — saved drafts, held proposals, reset time
Never lose staged work to an outage. If AiMY had drafted or staged an action when the service dropped, that state persists and the panel says so. Silently discarding it breaks the closed-loop guarantee that action state survives until the issue is resolved.
Type-to-Confirm

Delete "Aimy HQ"?

Modal + Wizard

The structured destination. When a decision needs several ordered inputs, formal review, or a record that outlives the conversation, it belongs in a modal wizard — Modal composed with Steps — not in the canvas. The canvas is a depth layer for investigation and judgement; it is not a crusade against forms.

Bulk edit across many rowsStructured workflowDense comparison and multi-select need dedicated controls
Single reversible changeNeither — direct actionAct in place and offer Undo
Compliance-governed configurationWizard + Type-to-ConfirmTop rung of the confirmation ladder
ElementClassNotes
Shell.modal-backdrop / .modalStandard modal. Unlike the canvas overlay this is blocking — the decision must be completed or cancelled
Progress.steps / .step.done / .active / default. Step count is fixed and visible up front — never reveal a fifth step at step four
Carried context.ctx-chipsContext handed in from the briefing or canvas arrives pre-filled and removable. The user does not re-enter what they already selected
Footer.modal-footerBack + Continue. The final step's primary is the real verb — "Submit dispute", never "Finish"
Confirmation Ladder

How much friction an action earns. Confirmation is proportional to consequence — over-confirming a reversible click trains people to dismiss dialogs, and under-confirming a governed change makes the dismissal habit expensive. Pick the rung from the blast radius, then use the component bound to it.

#ConsequenceConfirmationComponent
1 Reversible, single entity, low blast radius None — act, then toast with Undo AiMY Toast · .aimy-toast-undo
2 Reversible, multi-entity or cross-team Inline confirm in the action surface Confirmation popconfirm · .pop-actions
3 Irreversible, or changes governed configuration Reviewed action with an explicit diff and accept Governance Change Request + Decision Zone
4 Destructive, or affects scoring, compliance or permissions Reviewed action + typed confirmation + audit entry Type-to-Confirm + Audit Trail
Rung 1
Rung 2
Rung 3
Rung 4
The ladder runs one way. An action may be confirmed more heavily than its rung requires when the domain demands it, but never less. Where a rung's component does not yet exist for a given surface, the action does not ship — it is escalated as a gap.

Citation Preview

The middle rung of citation depth. Verification is layered so a reader skimming and a reader auditing can use the same answer without either being taxed: 1 inline marker → 2 source list → 3 this — the cited passage in context, without navigating away → 4 full source view. Rung 3 carries the most verification traffic, because it answers "does the source actually say that" at the cost of a hover.

Customers in the EU may request a refund within 30 days of purchase1 Refund eligibility — EU Verified …for orders placed through the EU storefront, customers may request a full refund within 30 days of purchase, provided the item has not been activated. Refunds are issued to the original payment method… policies.aimy.app · §4.2 , provided the item has not been activated2 Returns FAQ Due …activated items are handled case by case. An activated product is generally not eligible for return unless faulty… helpdesk.aimy.app .
Hover or focus a citation marker. Both previews are reachable with Tab.
ElementClassNotes
Wrapper.cite-wrapWraps the marker and its preview. position:relative
Marker.citeNeeds tabindex="0", role="button" and aria-describedby pointing at the preview. .is-flagged / .is-excluded when the source is not clean
Preview.cite-previewOpens on :hover and :focus-within. .is-open forces it for specimens. role="tooltip"
Header.cp-head / .cp-titleSource title plus its .trust-state — the trust of the source is what makes the citation worth trusting
Passage.cp-passage + <mark>The quoted span highlighted inside its surrounding text. Context is the point: a quote with no surroundings cannot be judged for cherry-picking
Per-citation actions.cite-actionOpen source · flag wrong. .is-flag for the destructive-tint hover, .is-flagged once raised
Feedback is captured per citation, not per answer. One bad citation inside an otherwise sound answer is the most actionable signal available and the most commonly discarded — a thumbs-down on the whole answer throws away which part was wrong. Flagging must route into the correction loop (open the source, edit, re-verify, reversible commit), not terminate in a rating.
A preview reachable only by mouse is not a verification affordance. The marker is focusable and the panel opens on :focus-within, so keyboard and screen-reader users get the same rung — which is why aria-describedby is required, not optional.
Answer Trust Disclosure

What every generated answer says about its own grounding: whether the sources behind it are verified, whether anything flagged contributed, and — the case that must never be silent — whether relevant content was withheld because it had expired. Without that last line a governance gap is indistinguishable from a gap in the corpus, and the user has no way to learn that the answer they need exists but has lapsed.

Clean grounding
Grounded in 3 verified sources, all reviewed within cadence.
Flagged source contributed
1 of 4 sources is due for review. Returns FAQ was last verified 84 days ago — treat that part of the answer as provisional.
Content excluded — the case that must not be silent
2 relevant sources were excluded because they are past their review date. This answer is thinner than the corpus can actually support.
“Refund eligibility — EU” expired 102 days ago · owner A. Mahfouz
Scope was narrowed by the user

Scope is set before the query runs, and stays visible throughout the answer — an answer read without knowing its scope is an answer that cannot be judged.

Scoped to Policies · official documentation only · verified content only. 14 sources considered, 3 cited.
ElementClassNotes
Panel.trust-disclosureSits with the answer, not in a drawer. .has-exclusion raises it to a warn surface — exclusion is the one case that earns visual weight
Row.td-row + .is-ok / .is-warn / .is-errIcon colour carries severity; .td-text stays at reading contrast so the sentence is never tinted into illegibility
Next step.td-actionRequired on the exclusion case. A disclosure with no route to fix it is a dead end, and dead ends fail the doctrine
Never mark content stale and keep serving it. A marking with no consequence is decorative and users correctly learn to ignore it. Exclusion is what makes trust state mean something; this component is what keeps exclusion honest by saying it out loud.

Governance Change Request

The heavyweight sibling of Suggestion Review. Use it when the proposed change touches governed configuration — thresholds, SLAs, scoring weights, routing rules, permissions — where the blast radius extends past the person reading it and the change must be auditable. Suggestion Review handles message-level edits; this handles operational commitments.

Decision Zone

Where a reviewed action is resolved. It states the decision being asked for, what happens as a result, and offers the three outcomes — Accept · Edit · Reject. Use it inside the canvas, inside a destination workflow, or at the foot of a change request. The user must never be able to reach the end of a proposal without seeing all three options.

Apply the revised P1 SLA to Teams Cairo, Nile, Delta and Aswan?

Takes effect at the start of the next scoring cycle. Historical scores are not recalculated. Reversible for 24 hours, after which reverting requires a new change request.

ElementClassNotes
Zone.decision-zoneRaised surface. Border tints ok/err once resolved
Prompt.dz-promptThe decision as a question. Names the affected entities explicitly — never "Apply changes?"
Consequence.dz-consequenceWhen it takes effect, what it does not touch, and how reversible it is. Mandatory before a first decision
Actions.dz-actionsAccept · Edit · Reject. .dz-spacer pushes the .work-state right
Meta.dz-metaWho proposed it, which role can decide, and that the decision is recorded
Edit is not optional. Offering only Accept and Reject forces the user to discard a nearly-right proposal. Acceptance, edit and rejection rates are all instrumented separately — an action with no edit path cannot be improved.

Canvas Overlay

A frosted-glass layer that fills .app-main when AiMY is in active conversation. Not a blocking modal, sidebar and topbar stay interactive. Enters at opacity 0 → 1 with a 280ms ease-out. Closes on Escape or the close button.

ℹ
The overlay uses backdrop-filter: blur(28px) saturate(1.4) brightness(0.85), it blurs and slightly dims the content behind it without adding a solid black dim. This preserves context while clearly separating the conversation space.

AiMY Toast

Two toast variants exist across the product. Both share the same base shape: fixed bottom-center, glass-frosted surface, 14px radius, slide-up + scale entrance at 220ms ease-spring. They differ in purpose and content.

Attention sort formula

attention = (100 − quality) × 0.5 + declineRate × 0.25 + (hasActivePlan ? −20 : 0) + Math.min(oldestActionDays, 30) × 0.5

Agents are sorted descending by attention score, highest attention (most at risk, least managed) first. A coaching plan deducts 20 points from the score, meaning managed agents naturally sink below unmanaged ones at the same quality level.

Lollipop Chart

Used in the Team view to compare all agents on a single goal. Each row is a horizontal axis with a stem line ending in a dot at the agent's score. A shared target line runs vertically across all rows. The dot's compound class encodes both color and trend direction: .ok-up / .ok-stable / .warn-stable / .warn-down / .err-down. Err-down dots pulse continuously via @keyframes lolli-pulse. Action buttons float absolutely over the right edge on hover.

Maps each behavioral goal to a horizontal axis inside the .behav-card. Three background zones (fail/watch/target) create a visual triage at a glance before reading any number. Score → axis position formula: left = (score − 40) / 60 × 100%, maps the 40–100% score range to the full axis width.

Heatmap

Two distinct heatmap components are used in the scorecards. Variant A (.heatmap-card) is a <table>-based goal × agent matrix in the Team view, agents as columns, goals as rows, each cell a colored score chip. Variant B (.heatmap-grid) is a CSS-grid coaching frequency heatmap, agents as rows, weeks as columns, showing at a glance which agents have been coached and when.

.ds-goal-six-gridgrid, repeat(6, 1fr), gap 12px; → 3 cols at <1400pxAlways exactly 6 tiles, one per core goal. If fewer goals, leave empty tiles rather than changing column count.

Behavioral goal Breakdown

The .behav-card is the primary goal breakdown surface on the agent scorecard. It has two co-present views: a dot plot (scores mapped to a horizontal axis with zone bands) and a compact list (.behav-list-compact) below it showing every goal as a numbered row with score, trend, and a hover-revealed action button. The two views are linked, clicking a dot plot marker highlights the corresponding row, and clicking a row opens a goal detail drawer inline.

Variant 1, Bar row (summary mode)

Used in the team view and overview contexts where the dotplot is not shown. Each goal is a flex row: label + full-width progress bar on the left, percentage + trend on the right.

Coaching Card

A rich canvas card that AiMY injects into the AiMY Canvas thread to deliver a coaching recommendation. Three action buttons, Accept, Defer (with snooze picker), Dismiss. Once actioned, the card transitions to a terminal state (accepted = green header; deferred = warn state pill) and hides the actions. Uses backdrop-filter: blur(8px) for the frosted glass surface.

Memory Panel

AiMY's persistent knowledge surface for a specific agent. Sits at the top of the agent scorecard, above the goal grid. Shows how long AiMY has been tracking the agent, accumulated evidence stats, the primary detected pattern, a trajectory confidence bar, and an expandable full detection timeline. Styled with an AI gradient tint (blue→teal) and a top-edge gradient shimmer line via ::before. The .memory-cue pill is a compact variant used inside the .ai-insight-panel header to signal session continuity.

AiMY has been tracking Omar for 5 months Updated 4 min ago
142 Interactions observed
89 Evaluations scored
47 Follow-up SOP misses
1 Coaching with confirmed improvement
AiMY first detected the follow-up SOP gap in W5 (Feb 18), 8 weeks before the quality score crossed below 70%. The pattern is consistent across email and chat, not concentrated in one channel.
Trajectory confidence
84%
Based on 8-week stable pattern across 2 channels · comparable to 3 similar historical cases

goal Detail Drawer

An inline expand panel that opens inside .behav-card between the dot plot and the compact list when a marker or row is clicked. It slides down via max-height animation (0 → 600px, 200ms ease-spring) and renders the goal number badge, full question title, score, mini progress bar, explanation body, and action buttons. The wrapper #goalDetailDrawer is permanently in the DOM. Content is injected by JS.

1 Did the agent set clear next steps and follow-up timeline? 47%
In 53% of evaluated interactions, the agent concluded without confirming next steps or a follow-up timeline with the customer. This is the primary driver of the current quality score decline, missing follow-up SOPs have a 0.6× correlation with CSAT drop in this team's historical data.

Drop Zone

The file upload zone used when ingesting evaluation files into a source. Default state: dashed border, ghost bg, centred icon + headline. Hover and .drag-over state: brand-blue border tint. Accepts tabindex="0" and keyboard activation. A .di-format-info strip below shows supported formats, max file size, and encoding requirements.

Drop files here, or browse
Evaluations, transcripts, or structured data files
Formats accepted
.csv .json .xlsx
Max file size 50 MB per file
Encoding UTF-8
ElementClassNotes
Zone.di-dropzoneborder:1.5px dashed rgba(255,255,255,0.1); border-radius:14px; padding:36px 24px 32px; text-align:center; cursor:pointer. tabindex="0" for keyboard access
Hover / drag.di-dropzone:hover, .di-dropzone.drag-overBrand-blue border + subtle bg tint. JS adds .drag-over on dragenter, removes on dragleave
Visual.di-dz-visualflex, centered, margin-bottom:16px. Wraps the upload icon ring
Headline.di-dz-headline13px/600, --d100, margin-bottom:6px. .di-browse inline span uses brand color + underline
Sub text.di-dz-sub12px, --d500
Format strip.di-format-infomargin-top:14px, ghost bg + hairline border, 10px radius, flex-column gap 10px
Format row.di-format-rowflex space-between, gap 8px
Label.di-format-label11px/500, --d500
Value.di-format-val11px, --d300
Format chips.di-format-chipsflex, gap 4px. Each .di-chip: 10px/600, ghost bg, 5px radius
Upload Queue

Each file dropped or selected becomes a .di-qitem card in the queue. A 2px progress bar uses the AI gradient while in-progress, then snaps to --ok (complete) or --err (failed). The cancel button turns red on hover. .di-qitem-status renders "Uploading…", "Complete ✓", or "Failed ✕" with semantic color modifiers. The queue header holds a title + a "Clear completed" text button.

Queue header.di-queue-headerflex space-between, margin-bottom:12px. .di-section-title (11px/700 uppercase --d400) + .di-text-btn (ghost "Clear completed")
Queue item.di-qitemGhost bg + hairline border, 9px radius, 12px 14px padding, margin-bottom:8px
Item header.di-qitem-hdflex, gap 8px, margin-bottom:8px. Holds name + size + cancel btn

Status text.di-qitem-status10px, --d500. Add .ok: --ok. Add .err: --err
AiMY Actions Strip

A blue-tinted contextual action strip shown after a successful upload. AiMY surfaces 3–5 suggested next steps as pill chips. Each chip fires a specific action when clicked (map columns, validate schema, preview data, schedule sync). The strip sits above the pipeline table and is dismissed after all actions are taken or the user closes it.

AiMY suggests
ElementClassNotes
Strip wrapper.di-aimy-actionsflex, flex-wrap, gap 8px, padding:16px 18px; margin-bottom:32px. Blue tint bg + border, 12px radius
Label row.di-aimy-actions-labelwidth:100%, 10px/700, uppercase, brand-blue tint color, margin-bottom 6px. Holds AiMY logo SVG + "AiMY suggests"
Chip.di-aimy-chipBrand-blue tinted pill, ghost bg + border. 11px/500, gap 6px. Hover: darker tint. SVG icon opacity:0.7
Sync Events

A chronological list of recent sync runs for the selected source. Each event is a flex row: a 7px status dot, a timestamp, and an outcome text. Read-only. Used in the source detail panel to show recent activity at a glance. Failed events expose a .di-failed-item card with error type, message, and retry/dismiss actions.

Today, 06:00 2,847 records synced
Yesterday, 06:00 Failed, auth error
May 7, 06:00 3,104 records synced
Zendesk API. May 8, 06:00
Auth error
Token expired, re-authenticate to resume scheduled syncs.
06:02 AM
ElementClassNotes
Event row.di-sync-eventflex, gap 14px, padding:11px 0; border-bottom:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.05). Last child: no border
Status dot.di-sync-dot.di-sync-ok/.di-sync-fail7px circle. ok=--ok, fail=--err
Timestamp.di-sync-time--d300, flex:1
Outcome.di-sync-out.ok/.fail12px/600. ok=--ok, fail=--err
Failed item card.di-failed-itemerr-tinted bg + border, 10px radius. flex row: icon + info + actions
Failed ID.di-failed-id13px/600, --d100
Error type.di-failed-type11px/600, --warn
Error message.di-failed-msg12px, --d400, line-height:1.5
Timestamp.di-failed-ts10px, --d500, margin-top:5px
Actions.di-failed-actionsflex, gap 4px, flex-shrink:0. Each .di-icon-btn: ghost, 6px radius, 6px padding
Config Modal + Add Source Wizard

Two modal variants share the same .di-modal shell: the Config modal (edit an existing source, tab-based: Connection / Sync settings / Danger zone) and the Add Source wizard (multi-step flow with a .di-wiz-steps progress indicator). Both use background:#1a2330, entrance animation mIn (translateY(10px)+scale(0.97) → identity, 260ms). Size variants: default 480px, .di-modal-lg 560px, .di-modal-sm 400px.
